explain.say: Here is a fun secret: your whole body can help you learn letters! Big moves first, then small moves. Look at the steps on the board. Let us try the letter o together.

faq.a: Sky writing means drawing a letter really big in the air with your whole arm. Big moves help your body learn the shape.

faq.q: What can I trace letters in?
faq.a: Sand, salt, rice, shaving foam, play dough or a steamy window. Anything you can draw in with one finger.
asks: What can I use for tracing?

faq.q: What if my small letter looks wobbly?
faq.a: That is normal and fine! Find one good thing about it, then try once more. A teacher or grown-up can trace with you if you like.
Big moves let you feel the whole shape with your arm, your eyes and your voice at once. Then the small version feels familiar.

faq.q: Do I need to say the moves out loud?
faq.a: It really helps. Saying start at the top, round and back while you move links your words and your hand together.

facts: Learning through several senses at once, like seeing, saying and moving, is called multisensory learning.
Many teachers use sand trays and writing in the air to practise letter shapes.
